Our formal Carbon Reduction Plan includes the following targets and actions: • Net Zero Operational Emissions by 2035: We are working towards eliminating all operational (Scope 1 and 2) greenhouse gas emissions, with interim reduction milestones to be established following our baseline carbon audit. • Whole Value Chain Climate Action: We are working towards significant reductions across our full value chain (Scope 3), including suppliers, logistics, product use, and end-of-life impacts, with a long-term aspiration of net zero emissions by 2040, subject to technology availability, supplier engagement, and industry collaboration. • Fossil Fuel Phase-Out: We aim to phase out fossil fuel use at operational sites by 2028 through electrification, efficiency improvements, and renewable energy sourcing, where technically and economically feasible. • Recycled and Recyclable Packaging by 2027: We are working towards transitioning all product packaging to fully recycled and recyclable materials to reduce waste and resource depletion, in line with product performance and safety requirements. • Recycled Content in Core Products: We are committed to increasing recycled content in our portable power stations and related products, targeting at least 50% by 2030 and greater than 95% where technically feasible by 2040, in line with product performance and safety requirements. • Annual Carbon Audits and Public Reporting: We conduct rigorous annual carbon footprint audits and disclose progress transparently in our sustainability reports to stakeholders. • Paperless Organisation: Minimising paper use through digital operations and documentation. • Sustainable Travel: Prioritising train travel where possible, minimising air miles, and optimising vehicle efficiency including regular maintenance and light load practices. • Green Energy Use: Sourcing renewable electricity at all applicable sites. • Shipping Imports by Sea: Wherever feasible, imports are shipped rather than flown, significantly reducing transportation emissions. (“APKI”) is committed to minimising the environmental impact of our operations by implementing effective waste management practices. This Waste Management Policy reflects our dedication to reducing waste generation, promoting reuse and recycling, and ensuring the responsible and compliant disposal of waste across all areas of our business. This policy applies to all employees, contractors, suppliers, and operational sites of APKI. APKI will manage waste in accordance with applicable UK waste legislation and regulatory guidance, with particular regard to the Environmental Protection Act 1990, the Environment Act 2021, the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013 (as amended), and the Hazardous Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2005 where relevant. 2. Purpose The purpose of this policy is to: ● Establish clear guidelines and responsibilities for waste reduction, reuse, and recycling. ● Ensure compliance with all applicable UK environmental and waste legislation, regulations, permits, and guidance, and to take account of wider good practice principles where relevant. ● Promote sustainable, circular economy principles in waste management across our operations and value chain. 3. Scope This policy covers all waste generated by APKI, including but not limited to: ● Production and manufacturing waste (including hazardous and non-hazardous wastes). Document number:APKI19 Version: V3 Date: 23/7/26 1 ● Packaging materials. ● Office and administrative waste. ● End-of-life product components, specifically Ze-Gens and related equipment. ● Waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE), batteries where applicable, and any associated packaging or component waste arising from APKI products. 4. Key Principles 4.1 Waste Reduction ● Efficient Resource Use: Promote optimised materials and resource consumption, implementing lean manufacturing and design-for-environment principles to minimise waste. ● Process Improvement: Use data-driven approaches and employee engagement to identify and implement process improvements that reduce waste. ● Circular Economy: Embed circular economy thinking by designing out waste at source and enabling product lifecycle extension where feasible. 4.2 Waste Reuse and Recycling ● Comprehensive Recycling Programme: Operate and maintain robust recycling schemes for key materials including paper, cardboard, plastics, metals, glass, and electrical/electronic waste (WEEE) in accordance with UK and international recycling standards. ● Design for Recyclability: Ensure that products and packaging are designed to facilitate disassembly, material separation, and reuse or recycling at end of life. ● Supplier Collaboration: Collaborate with suppliers to encourage the use of recycled, recyclable, and reusable materials and packaging. ● Where APKI is a producer or distributor of electrical and electronic equipment in the UK, it will comply with applicable WEEE obligations, including registration, financing Document number:APKI19 Version: V3 Date: 23/7/26 2 arrangements, marking, information provision, and record retention, as required by law. 4.3 Responsible Disposal • Hazardous Waste Management: Safely manage and dispose of hazardous waste in full compliance with the Hazardous Waste (England and Wales) Regulations 2005 and other applicable legal requirements, using appropriately authorised waste carriers, brokers, and treatment facilities. • Electronic Waste (E-Waste): Partner with appropriately authorised and competent ewaste recyclers and service providers, ensuring compliance with applicable UK WEEE requirements and environmentally sound recycling and disposal practices. • Legal Compliance: Maintain strict adherence to all applicable waste management, transport, storage, transfer, treatment, and disposal requirements relevant to APKI’s operations. 5. Specific Actions 5.1 Waste Segregation ● Onsite Segregation: Implement and maintain effective waste segregation systems at all APKI facilities to separate recyclables from non-recyclable and hazardous wastes. ● Awareness Raising: Promote the importance to employees and contractors of waste segregation protocols, recycling importance, and correct disposal procedures. 5.2 Recycling and Reuse Initiatives ● End-of-Life Management: Develop and maintain take-back schemes and recycling pathways for Ze-Gens and other end-of-life product components. ● Partnerships: Work with accredited recycling firms and organisations to maximise environmentally sound recovery and reuse of waste materials. ● Targets and KPIs: Establish measurable waste reduction and recycling targets, regularly monitor performance, and publicly report progress to drive accountability. Continuous Improvement ● Policy Review: Review and update the Waste Management Policy annually or as required to incorporate evolving legislation, technological advances, and industry best practices. ● Innovation Encouragement: Foster a culture of innovation by encouraging employees and suppliers to propose new ideas and technologies for waste minimisation and circularity. ● Sustainable Goals: Align waste management efforts with wider corporate sustainability objectives, including net-zero carbon commitments and resource efficiency targets. 7. Communication ● Policy Dissemination: Ensure this policy is communicated clearly and regularly to all employees, contractors, suppliers, and relevant stakeholders. ● Stakeholder Engagement: Actively engage with customers, suppliers, regulators, and local communities to promote awareness and cooperation on waste management and sustainability initiatives. WEEE Regulation Notice Overview of WEEE Regulations The Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013, as amended, set out the current UK legal framework for the management of waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE). These regulations apply to relevant producers, distributors, retailers, and other parties involved in placing electrical and electronic equipment on the UK market and managing waste electrical equipment. The regulations place specific obligations on producers and distributors of electrical and electronic equipment, including registration, financing or arranging appropriate collection and treatment routes where applicable, product marking, customer information, and recordkeeping Why WEEE Matters Electrical and electronic waste is a significant and growing waste stream. Improper handling or disposal of WEEE can lead to the release of hazardous substances and the loss of valuable materials that could otherwise be recovered, reused, or recycled. Our Commitment At APK Industries Ltd. (“APKI”), we recognise our obligation as a producer and supplier of electrical equipment to minimise the environmental impact of our products throughout their lifecycle. In compliance with WEEE regulations, we: ● Provide take-back, collection, or other compliant return arrangements for eligible endof-life APKI electrical products in accordance with applicable UK WEEE obligations and the business model under which the products are supplied. ● Ensure that all applicable products are marked with the crossed-out wheeled bin symbol, indicating that they should be collected separately from general waste and not disposed of in landfill. This symbol is required for products placed on the market on or after 13th August 2005. Document number:APKI20 Version: V3 Date: 23/7/26 1 Customer Information and Responsibilities ● Customers should not dispose of waste electrical and electronic equipment with unsorted general waste. apki-whistleblower-policy.pdf: APK Industries Ltd. Whistle Blower Policy 1. Introduction APKI Industries Ltd. (“APKI”) is dedicated to designing and manufacturing Zero Emission Generators (ZE-Gens), also known as Portable Power Stations (PPSs), delivering reliable and sustainable energy solutions worldwide. We believe access to energy is a fundamental right and are committed to innovation, environmental stewardship, and community empowerment. To uphold these values and ensure integrity across all operations, APKI has established this Whistle Blower Policy to encourage reporting of wrongdoing and protect those who raise concerns in good faith. This policy is intended to support compliance with UK whistleblowing protections under the Employment Rights Act 1996, as amended by the Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998, and reflects current UK government and Acas guidance. 2. Purpose This policy aims to: ● Encourage employees, contractors, suppliers, and stakeholders to report illegal, unethical, or improper conduct. ● Provide a safe, accessible, and confidential mechanism for raising concerns without fear of retaliation. ● Support a culture of honesty, transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement. ● Explain how whistleblowing differs from a personal grievance, which should normally be raised under APKI’s grievance or complaints procedures. 3. Scope Document number:APKI21 Version: V3 Date: 23/7/26 1 This policy applies to workers and other relevant persons connected with APKI’s activities, including employees, certain agency workers, trainees, contractors, consultants, and other individuals who may be covered by UK whistleblowing protections depending on the circumstances. Suppliers and external stakeholders may also raise concerns under this policy, although statutory whistleblowing protection may not apply in all cases. 4. Definition of Whistle Blowing Whistleblowing involves reporting information that the individual reasonably believes is in the public interest and tends to show one or more types of wrongdoing: ● Fraud, theft, embezzlement, or financial irregularities. ● Breaches of laws, regulations, or APKI policies. ● Corruption, bribery, or unethical business practices. ● Health and safety risks to employees, customers, or the public. ● Environmental damage or breaches of environmental law. ● Sexual harassment. ● Deliberate concealment of any of the above. ● Any other unlawful, unethical, or improper conduct. A personal employment complaint that only affects the individual making the report may be more appropriately handled under APKI’s grievance procedure unless it also raises a matter of wider public interest. 5. Reporting Procedure 5.1 Initial Reporting ● Concerns should be raised promptly when discovered. ● Reports may be made verbally or in writing. ● The designated Whistle Blower Officer is the Director, Alan Greig. Document number:APKI21 Version: V3 Date: 23/7/26 2 ● Contact details: Email: alan@apkindustries.com Phone: +44(0)3002003830 Reports should include, where possible, the nature of the concern, relevant dates, names, evidence available, and whether the matter has already been raised elsewhere. 5.2 Confidentiality and Anonymity ● All disclosures will be treated with strict confidentiality. The identity of the whistleblower will be protected unless required by law or with the individual’s consent. ● Anonymous reports are accepted; however, providing contact details can enhance the investigation’s effectiveness and allow for feedback. ● Information will only be shared with those who need to know in order to assess, investigate, or take action on the disclosure. 5.3 Alternative Reporting Channels ● Where appropriate, and if preferred, concerns may be raised in writing and sent to APK Industries, Sparkhouse, Rope Walk, Lincoln LN6 7DQ ● Workers may also seek advice from Acas, Protect, a trade union representative, legal adviser, or report to an appropriate prescribed person where the law allows. 6. Investigation Process 6.1 Assessment ● Upon receipt, the Whistle Blower Officer will assess the allegation’s validity and severity promptly to determine investigation steps. ● APKI will acknowledge receipt where possible and explain the next steps and likely process to the reporting person. 6.2 Fair and Impartial Investigation Document number:APKI21 Version: V3 Date: 23/7/26 3 ● Investigations will be conducted impartially, respecting principles of natural justice. ● Relevant parties may be interviewed, and evidence reviewed, maintaining confidentiality. ● Reasonable efforts will be made to conclude investigations in a timely manner. ● A whistleblower may be accompanied by a colleague, trade union representative, or other appropriate support person at any formal meeting where reasonable 6.3 Outcome and Actions ● Outcomes will be documented, and where appropriate, corrective actions will be implemented. ● Actions may include disciplinary measures, policy updates, procedural changes, or reporting to authorities. 6.4 Feedback to Whistleblower ● Where the whistleblower identifies themselves, and subject to confidentiality and legal constraints, they will receive feedback on the investigation’s outcome and any subsequent actions. 7. Protection Against Retaliation ● APKI prohibits retaliation, harassment, victimisation, dismissal, or any other detriment against a person who raises a concern that they reasonably believe is in the public interest and is made through an appropriate channel. ● Anyone found to be retaliating will face disciplinary action, up to and including dismissal or contract termination. ● APKI commits to supporting whistleblowers and maintaining a culture where concerns can be raised without fear. 8. Responsibilities 8.1 Whistleblowers Document number:APKI21 Version: V3 Date: 23/7/26 4 ● All personnel are encouraged and expected to report genuine concerns promptly. It is important that disclosures are made in good faith and not for malicious purposes. 8.2 Management and Director ● The Director (Alan Greig) is accountable for managing reports and investigations under this policy. ● Management at all levels must ensure awareness of this policy and support its enforcement impartially. ● Where a concern relates to the Director or would be inappropriate to report to the Director, the concern should be escalated to another senior officer, legal adviser, or an appropriate prescribed person. 8.3 Communication ● APKI will communicate this policy internally on a regular basis to ensure understanding and accessibility. ● Training on whistleblowing awareness and procedures will be provided to employees and managers as appropriate. ● This policy will be included in induction arrangements and reviewed regularly in line with Acas guidance. 9. Policy Review ● This policy will be reviewed annually or more frequently if needed to ensure it reflects legal requirements, best practices, and organisational needs. ● Updates will be communicated promptly to all stakeholders. For any questions or to raise a concern under this policy, please contact: Alan Greig, Director Email: alan@apkindustries.com Phone: +44(0)7990 892733 Document number:APKI21 Version: V3 Date: 23/7/26 5
